To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a hardware/software co- design for the read-out of a KID array, and the system was tested successfully.
we developed the Front-End Electronics for a 128 KID array and the DAQ system that interfaces the Front-End to the detector.
the DAQ and the Front- End electronics for an array Kinetic Inductances Detectors (KID) are developed and tested successfully.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new type of detector, the Kinetic Inductances Detector, and with the design of a new DAQ system, based on a microprocessor and on a FPGA.
the development of an integrated system, based on KIDs and the DAQ system described, for the detection of cosmic ray particles.
the development of an integrated system for the detection of radiation, based on superconductive detectors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the developed DAQ system has been successfully implemented and tested.
the DAQ and the Front- End electronics developed are suitable to read-out and control an array of KIDs.
we have designed a complete DAQ system for an array of KIDs, which has been validated through simulations and tests.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we designed and built a DAQ system that is suitable for the read out of an array of KID.
we designed and implemented a DAQ system for KIDs.
we have designed a DAQ system for an array of KIDs, which can operate in the frequency band of 1.2–1.8 GHz.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DAQ system we built is a flexible, low-cost and easy to use solution for KIDs readout.
a KID array can be easily read-out by a commercial FPGA board, which can be interfaced to the KIDs by a commercial DAC and ADC board.
the DAQ is a crucial part of a KIDs system and that a proper DAQ can be designed to meet the requirements of a specific experiment.
